All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5857 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • Sources indicate that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

Sources indicate that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 new players, but did not upgrade two of the most notable positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the major difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

According to recent reports, zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Recent findings suggest that suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

It has been revealed that spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Sources indicate that asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

Sources indicate that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he said: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

Recent findings suggest that it was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

Jackson was not the only Villa latest boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Sources indicate that johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

Substitute Mohammed Kudus was correctly denied an equaliser following a VAR check before Jackson’s goal and a brilliant strike from Emiliano Buendía that effectively clinched a first league win of the season for Villa.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Unai Emery, the head coach, spent years watching Martínez and Ollie Watkins win games for Villa with decisive actions, and is hoping this was evidence that Suzuki and Jackson can do the same for him.

“They are here for it [making the same impact],” Emery remarked. “His commitment, Zion is really very good. His commitment, Nico Jackson as well is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively, how they can help us with their qualities, and how we can collectively exploit our best performance.

Sources indicate that “Today we made one clear step forward. Zion is keeping his performance like he did before. Jackson today clearly improved his performance. This is the way forward and the example for the other players.

“Manzambi played a good match, but he’s not yet understanding everything we need on the field with our positioning. He’s a fantastic player and must feel free playing to try to exploit himself and his qualities. But, of course, always under our structure.”.

Speaking after the match, former Spurs man Joe Cole was critical of the club’s summer business which has left them without an out-and-out goalscorer and a weak defence.

"You can't rule them out of a relegation battle"Steven Gerrard and Joe Cole have major concerns for Spurs 😬🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/JivM5pNfM9.

Plenty of fans leaving before full-time...

and heartbreak for the ones that stayed...

"It's a long international break, you don't want to be in the bottom three"John McGinn on the 'relief' for Aston Villa to pick up their first league win of the season 😅🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Gl38uj1pig.

We’ve got a three-week international break after this weekend, so there’s a little while before both teams will be back in action, but this is what awaits them when they return:.

vs Man Utd (A) - Oct 10th, 5.30pm.

vs Coventry (H) - Oct 19th, 8pm.

vs Chelsea (A) - Oct 24th, 5.30pm.

vs Crystal Palace (H) - Oct 31st, 5.30pm.

vs Brentford (H) - Oct 10th, 3pm.

vs Fenerbahce (H) - Oct 14th, 8pm.

vs Newcastle (A) - Oct 17th, 5.30pm.

vs Man City (H) - Oct 24th, 12.30pm.

"The fans deserved the win." 👏Emi Buendia shows his appreciation to Aston Villa supporters after a much-needed victory 💜🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Qjn6RihNGD.

John McGinn is also speaking to TNT now, so we’ll get you his quotes soon.

Villa only had seven touches in the Spurs box in that second half, but that was enough to secure two goals and all three points.

Spurs thought they had pulled themselves level while Villa were only 0-1 up after 60 minutes, but VAR judged Robertson to be offside.

Spurs thought they had their first Premier League goal of the season...Until VAR ruled it out for offside 😬 pic.twitter.com/FJsrLhm0FG.

Emi Buendia, that is a BEAUTIFUL strike 😮‍💨📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nNplbL7mpd.

Possession: Spurs 64% vs 36% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 31 vs 18.

Aston Villa have jumped with their first win of the season, while Tottenham have sunk back into the relegation zone.

Recent findings suggest that “We were looking for this win from the beginning. We had a really difficult start of the season in terms of results and not finding our best football but I think today we highlighted a really good character.”.

And that is it! A second late consolation goal is not enough to stem the boos from the stands.

In a recent development, late action from Tottenham but they leave it too late to get a result. Another loss at home sends De Zerbi back to the drawing board.

This will be the last of the game probably as Maddison is fouled outside the area for Spurs’ third free kick in quick succession. Robertson takes it and sends a perfect delivery to the back post.

It is the first one that Mings has been caught under and van Hecke gets there to send it past Suzuki.

Another foul for Spurs, on the corner of the box. Maddison to take again and Mings does great work to judge the path of the ball and head it out from the centre of the box.

Recent findings suggest that callagher gets the ball in midfield and feeds Savio on the left who pulls it back. The ball he sends into the box is cleared from a crowd of bodies by Barkley.

Though Savio takes the corner quickly, it comes out to the edge of the area. Bentancur rises to meet the ball lifted in to the box and flicks it on behind himself towards goal, and it just goes wide of the post.

Sources indicate that maddison stands over it, and goes for goal, curling it very well, though Suzuki is in the right place to punch it away. It falls to Kudus, whose follow-up is a much less exciting effort, sailing over the bar.

We will have seven minutes added on here.

It has been revealed that kudus has been fouled as he try to get forward. Spurs are still looking for a second goal and Savio is fouled on the left side of the box. Cash gets a card for it and it is a very interesting position, not far from the touchline.

It has been given as a Gallagher goal for now.

But it is just too little too late for Spurs. No celebration from De Zerbi and hardly a cheer from the fans remaining in the stadium.

Tammy Abraham has come on by the way, replacing Jackson for the final few minutes.

It has been revealed that A consolation for Spurs! They have their first league goal to almost no reaction from their fans.

Kudus cuts the ball back and it is not clear whether Cash or Gallagher get there first to poke it home.

It looks like a Cash own goal...

The Spurs fans are leaving in droves. All you can hear in the stadium now are the rejoicing Villa fans.

McGinn comes off for Ross Barkley and Kamara off for Mbaye.

Spurs replace Bentancur and Tonali with Lucas Bergvall and Connor Gallagher.

This is absolutely what Villa needed. They have been great out of possession, just patient and disciplined and taking their chances when they come.

This is going to be a long three weeks for De Zerbi. Spurs have not managed a shot on target in the half, despite all their dominance on the ball.

That must be the final nail in the coffin for Spurs.

Recent findings suggest that gomes makes a great run, sending the ball out to McGinn on the right win. Rather than send the ball in to the box, he sends it out to the edge of the area and there is Buendia. He runs on to it late, finding the top left corner with an immaculate strike.

The Spurs fans are flooding out.

Villa have been calm without the ball in this half. Spurs have dominated possession but Villa have been very organised in defence.

Gray is fouled 35 yards out and Maddison takes the free kick. It only meets the first man in the box, who is Ruggeri, who clears.

Spurs are having no luck and have just not been able to get themselves in front.

Sources indicate that marmoush gets the ball from Maddison on the edge of the area and takes a shot on the turn. It’s blocked by Lindelof for a corner.

Savio takes again but Suzuki punches it away in the centre of the box.

Kudus tries a ball from on the right of the area, looking to find Robertson at the back post but Suzuki again comes confidently to claim it.

Change for Villa as Manzambi comes off to make way for George Hemmings.

17 minutes for Spurs to find a goal...or two.

Tonali comes close! From 35 yards out, the Italian takes a touch to shift it onto his left foot and sends a curling effort towards goal. Suzuki dives but can’t get there and the ball just whistles past the top far corner of the goal.

At least Spurs’s heads haven’t gone down but they still have nothing to show for it.

Savio sends a cross in from the right but there’s only Buendia in the box to meet it. He sends it out and Jackson finds himself with it again on the left side. Villa’s play breaks down but they are not backing down.

Well it’s gone from bad to worse for Spurs.

Jackson gets his first goal for his new club and van Hecke has got to do better there.

According to recent reports, he gets on the end of an incredible long ball from Suzuki, and van Hecke does not get close enough to challenge him. He takes a touch to get it past van de Ven and sends it past Kinsky from the edge of the box into the bottom corner. The keeper gets a hand on it but it comes in off the post, almost in slow motion.

James Maddison will be coming on shortly.

Tonali sends a ball across to Savio on the right corner of the box, and his low ball in goes out the back for a corner.

Solanke can’t control it as it comes in and that will be his last action before he makes way for Maddison.

Marmoush goes down on the edge of the box, pushed by Joao Gomes, earning a free kick.

Sources indicate that robertson and Marmoush standing over it, just on the left of the area. Robertson is the one to take, lifting it towards the back post but Suzuki comes out to claim easily.

Recent findings suggest that so close for Spurs! A fantastic run from Robertson but the defender strays just offside just outside the box. He takes the ball down to the back line, drawing Suzuki off his line, and it is crossed back past the keeper and bundled over the line by Kudus.

Huge cheers before VAR takes a look. The wait goes on.

It has been revealed that ruggeri intercepts a loose ball in midfield and makes a run down the left side. He lifts a ball towards the centre of the box, but Betancur beats the waiting Manzambi to it, bringing it down and nudging it towards his keeper.

Savio again on the right edge of the box lifts a ball across the box towards the back post, but Suzuki judges it well and comes off his line to claim it.

We’re back underway as Kinsky had to receive a bit of treatment there.

It has been revealed that tonali plays it in for Savio but it’s intercepted by a Villa shirt. It’s played out for Jackson on the left wing to have a run and he gets past van Hecke very easily to reach the edge of the area and take a shot – which goes high and wide.

Industry observers note that unai Emery warned Nicolas Jackson about getting unnecessary bookings yesterday after having to substitute him on a yellow card at half-time last week. 30 seconds into the second half, Jackson got a needless yellow car for stopping a free-kick being quickly taken. Emery pointed straight to his head when it happened.

Industry observers note that savio tries to find Bentancur as he makes a run down the centre of the field. The midfielder gets a head on it but it heads the wrong way.

Recent findings suggest that but the game is opening as Spurs push, and Villa go on the counter with Manzambi running down the left side. He feeds a ball through to Jackson who carries it into the box but Kinsky judges it well and comes out to block the shot.

Spurs are pressing very high now and Villa have dropped very deep, especially their midfield.

Savio tries to put a ball in to the box but it’s trapped by Manzambi who plays the ball out. Ruggeri gets the ball back in to midfield to Buendia, who tees up Manzambi for a run into the box. The Swiss international is closed down well though.

Time to see how Spurs will react after that goal.

There’s still plenty of fight left as Kudus sends the ball out to Savio, trying to get to the touchline to cross a ball back in but Ruggeri stays on him.

We’re back in action in north London.

Spurs: Mateus Fernandes for Mohammed Kudus.

Villa: Wan-Bissaka for Matty Cash.

And as I’m typing this , it’s an early yellow for Jackson for a silly foul. Here we go!

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

It looks like Mohammed Kudus will be on at half-time for football. He’s been going through his own half-time warm-up. Matt Cash has been doing the same for Villa, so maybe we will see him too.

Possession: Spurs 57% vs 44% Villa.

Touches inside opposition box: 14 vs 11.

In all fairness to Spurs, they have pushed for a goal all half and only been denied by some fantastic keeping from Zion Suzuki.

Here are some of the biggest saves of the half:.

Zion Suzuki with a double save to deny Spurs an opener 🧤📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/b7WITUtjf2.

Back-to-back huge saves from Zion Suzuki! 🤯📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/uXKkicEeer.

It has been revealed that predictably, there were boos from the home fans at half-time. That was the ninth half of Premier League football Spurs have failed to score in. They should have done and would have done if it weren’t for the heroics of Zion Suzuki in the Villa goal. Manzambi’s goal was only Villa’s second in the League this season and this is the first time they have led in a League game.

Spurs looking shaky now as they come close to conceding a second, seconds before the whistle finally blows.

Boos around the stadium as the players head down the tunnel. De Zerbi has work to do.

Spurs have not come from behind to win since November 2024.

This is a tall challenge now, as van Hecke is the first to go into the book for a foul on Jackson.

To rub salt in the wound, Spurs have a decent shout for a free kick on the edge of the box before that as Gomes pushes Mateus Fernandes as he makes a run into the box.

Well this is the last thing Spurs would have wanted. Minutes before half-time Manzambi puts the vistors in front.

Robertson slides to try and stop a ball going out for a corner but he only finds McGinn. He sends it into the box and finds Kamara, who takes a shot. It bounces towards goal and Manzambi pokes it past Kinsky for the lead.

Recent findings suggest that van de Ven is off the pitch on his feet, sporting an impressive bruise now. Spurs are down to 10 as they try to get the swelling down.

There will be five minutes added, though play is yet to resume as van de Ven receives treatment for a cut below his eye.

The last thing Spurs need now is to be forced into another defensive change after losing Porro.

Wan-Bissaka picks up the ball sent out to him on the wing by Manzambi, who is fouled by Marmoush.

The free kick is outside the area, but McGinn takes looking goalwards.

Mings makes the run looking to get his head on it, but van de Ven goes up with him and gets there first to clear it, though the Dutch international takes a blow to the head and goes down for treatment.

Joao Gomes races forward, sending the ball to Ruggeri on his left. He tries to put it in the box, but it goes out the back off Archie Gray for Villa’s first corner.

McGinn delivers but it comes off Solanke, who clears. No luck yet as we head towards half-time, despite plenty of action in front of goal.

Roberston again with a sliding cross that Lindelof sends out the back.

Another corner for Spurs, but it is headed away again by Mings, who gets up high. That’s Spurs’s seventh corner.

Great long ball from Robertson to try and find Marmoush but Suzuki comes far outside his area to control it with his chest on the bounce and play it away with his feet.

Sources indicate that villa get a free kick inside as Bentancur catches Manzambi, but the Swiss international goes down and receives some treatment on the pitch. He has to go off for a minute, but he is on his feet.

But Spurs come again and it’s Tonali this time. He takes a shot from outside the area, and would have beaten Suzuki low on the right, but the shot is just wide.

It has been revealed that spurs get a corner, delivered by Savio, and it’s headed on to Solanke at the back post. He heads it towards goal but it’s blocked by Wan-Bissaka. Cries for handball, but it’s cleared.

Marmoush makes a very well-timed run to get on a long ball from van Hecke, and does well to stay onside. But his first touch is not good enough and Suzuki can come to collect.

Recent findings suggest that jackson picks up a ball from Kamara, played over him into the Spurs half. He puts it into the centre of the field towards Buendia, who tees up Manzambi but his shot from distance sails over the bar.

Villa now having a spell. Manzambi gets onto a loose ball in midfield and lays it off to Buendia who feeds Jackson in the centre of the field. He does well to keep the ball down and turn round van Hecke to take a shot on the edge of the area, but he skews his shot wide.

He should be hitting the target at least from there but you can see how desperate both sides are to get their noses in front here.

Recent findings suggest that jackson gets around Gray and runs into the box on the left side. He pokes a ball through to Buendia, who takes a shot on goal at the near post, but Kinsky gets down to his left to stop the shot.

Sources indicate that mings almost causes a catastrophe for Villa as he and Lindelof close a loose ball down. Suzuki comes out to claim, but the defender pokes it towards him, almost past him under pressure and the keeper has to send it out the sideline.

Four huge saves by Suzuki as Spurs have had five early shots in total to Villa’s single shot on target. They are finding a lot of joy against the left side of Villa’s defence.

Fernandes has an attempt from distance, but drags his shot wide.

Well Spurs are really pushing for a goal!

In a recent development, it’s a perfect first involvement for Gray, as he times a perfect run to get behind Ruggeri to pick up a ball from Savio. He lets it run inside the box but it flashes across the face of goal, just tipped away by Suzuki.

Another attempt denied immediately after as Savio connects perfectly with the volley on the edge of the area, and Suzuki dives down to his left to parry away.

Incredible start for the Villa keeper and Spurs can smell a goal coming.

Spurs had started on the front foot, but let’s see how they handle this change.

Industry observers note that porro went straight down the tunnel when he went off. It was a problem with his left leg. That’s a blow for Spurs, as Porro offers an attacking threat.

Early concern for Spurs as Porro has gone down and is looking very frustrated. Archie Gray has gone out to warm up, but this is a huge blow for De Zerbi if Porro has to come off.

He had been missing due to a muscle injury but it’s not clear if that’s the issue here. He has been very good so far today, helping build play and bringing huge amounts of experience.

And a shot on target next for Villa as Manzambi has an effort from just inside the 18-yard box off his left foot, but Kinsky makes a relatively easy save as the ball boucnes towards him.

Villa get their first chance, as Jackson races down the left side but van de Ven is content to stay close and as no Villa players follow him into the box, van Hecke is the one who clears his cross into the box.

Suzuki has been good with his feet since joining Villa, but he’s kicked about three balls straight out of play so far today.

No wonder De Zerbi had his t-shirt pulled over his head. Tottenham looked certain to score their first Premier League goal of the season through Savio. Suzuki didn’t know too much about the first shot, which hit him, but reacted well to tip the second over.

Outstanding from the Villa keeper!

Tonali crosses a great ball in from the left and Savio has two great chances from close range but Suzuki blocks the first with his chest and tips the second over the bar.

The corner, delivered by Savio, is headed out by Mings and Villa keep control.

Suzuki plays a long ball out down the field, and as Jackson and van de Ven tussle to reach it, the defender is shoved to the floor and gets the free kick.

Sums up the early battles so far.

Spurs are putting a lot of pressure on Villa as they try and play the ball out, and McGinn loses the ball again in midfield. Spurs surge forward again but Mings gets his head onto the ball crossed into the box and Villa survive again.

In a recent development, savio takes but it is headed out. It falls to Porro outside the box who lifts another ball in, but the Villa line holds firm and clears for a throw in from the left side.

Marmoush tries to run into the box but a well-time challenge by Kamara gets the ball off him.

Villa lose the ball in midfield and it’s played up to Solanke. Lindelof comes across well but concedes a corner.

Tech Report: Gold for the West Bank: Meet Palestinian karate champ Mariam Bsharat

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat remarked.
  • Themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a massive win.
  • "It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"After the referee lifted my hand to show I'm now a two-time world champion, it was a very overwhelming feeling," Mariam Bsharat remarked. "Making history once is something, but making it twice is really something else. I felt very happy and I felt a substantial relief. Only I know how many sacrifices I made and how many hardships I needed to overcome.".

Themes of relief, joy and sacrifice are commonplace in the reflections of athletes after a massive win. In Mariam Bsharat's case, it's about more than just dedication to training and taking care of the body. The 17-year-old won her second under-21 World Karate Championship gold medal competing for the Palestine national team in Poland in October.

"It was everyday life, seeing people get killed around me and houses getting bombed," she told DW of her upbringing in the occupied West Bank.

"I faced challenges in transportation," Bsharat said. "I wasn't able to go from one city to another to be able to train with other people, so that I can actually prepare for competitions. I needed to travel to other countries like Jordan or Egypt ... which was very hard for me. And, financially, the support wasn't really the support an elite athlete needed.".

Growing up in Nablus, Bsharat had a narrow path to the top. But initially, it was her own reluctance that threatened to stop a champion career before it started.

"When I was a little kid, I did not really love it," said Bsharat, who competes in the division for fighters who weigh under 66 kilograms (145 pounds).

Sources indicate that "I started it because my family was in that sport," Bsharat remarked. "My father had a dojo, and my mother also did that sport. My siblings and my aunts and my uncles — it's a family thing. I started it because they were all doing it. In time, I started getting into it.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, family has been a constant source of comfort and inspiration for Bsharat. Her father and uncle have acted as manager and coach respectively. While her mother and siblings moved with Mariam to Hamburg, Germany, last year, her father remained in order to take care of his business, the dojo, though he visits and tries to be with his daughter in competitions. Integration has been made easier by her mastery of the language, taught to her by her German mother.

Bsharat has mixed feelings about leaving her homeland.

Sources indicate that "I'm thankful to be here because being in Germany opened lot of doors for me, and I think I have a brighter future here," Bsharat remarked. "But also being in Palestine was just my everyday life, and I loved it there. My family was around me, my friends were around me, and I just felt comfortable, which was a massive change coming here to Germany. I think every change comes with hardships.".

Recent findings suggest that as well as the obvious difficulties of living in an area occupied by Israel, there are particular challenges for sportspeople living in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, with access to facilities, travel and constant security fears among them. As such, very few people from the Palestinian territories become successful on the international sporting stage. That, Bsharat mentioned, gives her responsibilities that are unusual and heavy for a person of any age, let alone a 17-year-old.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that "Being an elite athlete in Palestine is something very special because not everybody in Palestine has that opportunity. There aren't really a lot of athletes that are elite and who win international medals,” Bsharat stated.

"So all that pressure from all the country and all the people, the family, the coaches are on me because I'm representing them, raising their flag,” she stated. "I sometimes even forget to fight for myself and actually think about myself.".

That has not yet proved a barrier to Bsharat, who is is ranked first in the world in her category by the World Karate Federation (WKF). With Palestine recognized by the International Olympic Committee, Bsharat would likely have been a contender to raise that flag in Los Angeles at the 2028 Olympics. But the sport was dropped from the Games in 2024.

It has been revealed that "The global karate community remains steadfast in our belief that the natural place for karate is within the Olympic Games, and we sincerely hope that the incongruence we suffered in Paris 2024 and LA 2028 will be corrected for Brisbane 2032, if not sooner," the WKF wrote in response to the decision in 2024. The sport was also taken off the slate for the recent Youth Games in Senegal.

Should karate return in Brisbane, Bsharat would likely be approaching her prime. In the meantime, she is looking forward to starting her journey as a senior when she turns 18. But she won't be hanging around.

"My goal is it to be a world champion at seniors, which is the hardest and the best thing you can achieve in karate," she stated.

"But winning an Olympic medal, being called Olympic champion or just representing my country with that flag [is a thought that] is just full of happiness and pride.".

The interview was conducted by Janek Speight.

Sources indicate that luciano Spalletti will not hold his eve-of-match press conference before Sunday's trip to Fiorentina. Juventus arrive on two straight wins, chasing fourth place, against a coach Spalletti has never beaten.

In a recent development, juventus will travel to Florence without the usual preview from their coach. Sunday’s game at the Franchi kicks off at 20:45. The squad got back to Turin overnight from the Netherlands. The reason given is the club’s crowded run of fixtures, TuttoJuve reported. It is the last game before the international break.

The run began with a 2-0 win over Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on 1 November. Kerim Alajbegovic scored in the 70th minute. Aged 19 years and 41 days, no foreign player had ever found the net at a younger age in a Serie A game between Juventus and Napoli.

Four days later, Juventus won 2-1 away at AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League. Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani scored. The result takes them to 10 points from four games in the competition. After the match, Spalletti described himself as very pleased with a solid team display against strong opponents. He felt his side should have added a third goal.

The league position still needs work. The club’s stated aim this season is fourth place, and Como currently hold that spot. The defence gives some grounds for confidence. Going back to last March, no side can match the Bianconeri’s tally of 12 shutouts. Roma are next on 11.

Industry observers note that vanoli and Spalletti have faced each other only twice as coaches. Both meetings were Fiorentina-Juventus fixtures last season. Last November they drew 1-1 at the Franchi. Filip Kostic gave Juventus the lead before Rolando Mandragora equalised with a long-range shot.

The hosts’ struggles on their own pitch offer Juventus an opening against a side yet to find its footing at home.

According to recent reports, the fixture carries plenty of history. Sunday’s game is the 175th Serie A meeting between the sides, according to the club’s statistical preview. Juventus have won 82, Fiorentina 37, and 55 have ended level. Juventus have scored 275 top-flight goals against Fiorentina. Two more would draw them level with Inter’s 277, the highest total by any side against the Viola.

Once the international break is over, Juventus’s next Serie A match is on 22 November.

Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
  • Sources indicate that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

Sources indicate that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

In this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old said last year of his former team-mate Messi.

Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most important players.

Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

Another promptly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

Inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

It has been revealed that ‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler noted shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

Recent findings suggest that across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

In a recent development, but who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

In this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

In a recent development, former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer claims. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

Industry observers note that ‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

Recent findings suggest that during his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

Sources indicate that spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another key step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

In a recent development, ‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer says. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

According to recent reports, the audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

In a recent development, ‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he notes. ‘He wants to achieve big things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

Industry observers note that the refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

It has been revealed that his strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Sources indicate that pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

In a recent development, united should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

It has been revealed that the sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

When Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

According to recent reports, it proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

According to recent reports, “It was a really good fight,” Alisson noted, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

It has been revealed that since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

Sources indicate that “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

According to recent reports, don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

Cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

According to recent reports, alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Recent findings suggest that “A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

It has been revealed that one, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

Recent findings suggest that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose stated. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

According to recent reports, speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola stated: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

In a recent development, jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that revealed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

"Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

In a recent development, "That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

Cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young noted on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose massive players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

Sunderland are still 5-3 down but have not given up the ghost. Surely the best match of the season so far?

Araujo gets his pocket picked in the corner but Jebbison cannot compose himself and blasts his cross off the other side of the pitch.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has mentioned and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

In a recent development, there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has stated that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he stated: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He stated: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, noted: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”.

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

According to recent reports, the Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 22 Nov 2026 13:39.

Newcastle United are reportedly interested in negotiating a swap deal with Juventus involving Nick Woltemade.

The Magpies earned a spirited 2-2 draw with leaders Arsenal on Saturday evening to end the day in 12th position in the Premier League table.

However, with just three wins in 11 league matches, Matthias Jaissle remains under pressure at St James' Park.

During the summer transfer window, the decision was taken to allow Woltemade to move on loan to Juventus.

That is despite Newcastle having paid £69m for the forward during the 2025 summer transfer window.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Newcastle chiefs are open-minded to allowing the Germany international to remain in Turin on a permanent basis.

Nevertheless, it is claimed that they would like to discuss a potential swap deal involving Francisco Conceicao.

That is despite the Portuguese winger said to remain as a favourite of Juve boss Luciano Spalletti.

Conceicao has contributed just one goal and one assist from his seven starts and two substitute outings in Serie A and the Europa League.

Meanwhile, Woltemade has an impressive five goals and three assists from seven starts and seven substitute appearances in the same competitions.

If Juventus wish to keep Woltemade on a permanent basis, they will need to generate funds or go down the player-exchange route.

Newcastle will not consider selling Woltemade for less than £50m, a figure that Juventus cannot meet at the present time.

Unless the Premier League club take an interest in another Juventus player, the Italian club may have to be open-minded to allowing Conceicao to leave, assuming that Woltemade's return in the final third is viewed more important.

  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one matter ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

With Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already noted he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, said in a note.

Recent findings suggest that "I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

Sources indicate that some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

According to recent reports, kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, stated the vote showed the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of significant tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

In a recent development, "This election reveals that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he stated. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

Sources indicate that if the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown mentioned, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

That sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

In a recent development, "Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

According to recent reports, trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard stated, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump remarked in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election glitch — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

It has been revealed that "You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard mentioned. "From a political point of view, that's the most key thing now.".

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he mentioned in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and concerns.

Sources indicate that yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another issue vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the newly introduced Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic challenges to secure his political survival.

"Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard mentioned. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

  • Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met.
  • According to recent reports, the numbers explain the concern.
  • According to recent reports, garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

According to recent reports, the numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

According to recent reports, garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

It has been revealed that fotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • "To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No.
  • "I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cristiano Ronaldo took to social media on Thursday to announce that he had played his last game for Portugal.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo noted in a video on his Instagram account.

"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world," Ronaldo said.

The former Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus forward represented his country 234 times, scoring 146 goals — making him the men's record-holder for ⁠international ​appearances and for international goals.

He captained Portugal ​to their first major trophy at ​Euro 2016 and led them to the 2019 and 2025 Nations League titles.

"It was not an easy decision, there are decisions that are not ​only with the head. They are also made with the heart," Ronaldo continued in the Instagram post.

"If I ever made you happy, ​if one of my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel ⁠proud ​of our country, then it ​was all worth it.".

He also thanked his family, the Portuguese people ​and the teammates, coaches and staff he worked with over his national ​team career.

The Portuguese Football Association (FPF) released a statement expressing its gratitude and respect for the player also known as "CR7.".

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" it read.

The FPF intends to organize a tribute "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much.".

It has been revealed that while his long-rival Lionel Messi ended his Argentina career with a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance may go down as Portugal's 1-0 win over Wales on September 24, depending on the nature of the tribute. Portugal coach Jorge Jesus left him on the bench for the following match and mentioned he wouldn't start the next one.

Ronaldo responded by walking out of the Portugal training camp. He was subsequently suspended and fined by the FPF, but he had been expected to return to Portugal for the November international break.

Like Messi, Ronaldo intends to continue his club career with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

Gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina. Spalletti's side now go into the international break outside the Champions League places, with their next home game brought forward by a day.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

According to recent reports, the hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Sources indicate that fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

Recent findings suggest that the closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Sources indicate that referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

According to recent reports, juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

At his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti mentioned he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything notable. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

Sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

It has been revealed that on TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and noted that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville says Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

It has been revealed that neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

In a recent development, it begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

Industry observers note that it is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

According to recent reports, that 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

It was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.
